review_notes:
I read the whole file. It never calls `simp`, `simp only`, `simpa` or `simp_all`. The proofs use only `rw`, `exact`, `show`, `calc`, `induction` and `infer_instance`. The new lemmas (`nsmul_eq_nsmulPt`, `nsmulPt_val`, `fst_comp_eq_schemeKerStr`, `nsmulPt_eq_one_of_factorsThrough`) are plain, correctly oriented equations that would not need `@[simp]`. Adding it to them would risk unwanted unfolding of `nsmulPt` and `L.nsmul`, so I recommend no change.

The only simp-related item is the long `attribute [-simp] …` line at the top. I spot-checked two of the removed lemmas. `schemeHomOverComp_id_left` (in Definitions/Def_AlgebraicGeometry_NeronModelEndomorphismExtension.lean) and `homOverId_coe` (in Definitions/Def_AlgebraicGeometry_NeronSpecialFibreRestriction.lean) are both `@[simp]` identity-style lemmas. Neither looks like a looping or competing rule. Because the file uses no simp, the line has no effect here. It looks like boilerplate that the repository applies in many files; the grep for `attribute [-simp]` found over 28,000 files. I found no evidence of a specific bad lemma, cycle, competing rule or unwanted expansion in this file, so I report no finding.

I did not check the 30 or so removed lemmas one by one. I also did not check whether other files depend on them, so a simp-set problem elsewhere in the repository remains possible.
